newsitem.title: USA: Global sees possible reduced profits.
newsitem.headline: Global sees possible reduced profits.

text.p: Global Outdoors Inc said the Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed that its financial statements be revised to defer certain revenue for lifetime memberships.
It said the proposed revision would "substantially reduce the revenues and profits of the company."

The revenue recognition policy relates to the company's Lost Dutchman's Mining Camp Club. The company said it currently recognizes sales revenue upon execution of a membership sales contract and receipt of cumulative payments of at least 10 percent of the sales price.
The company also provides a 10 percent allowance for doubtful accounts and discounts the contracts over the contractual repayment period.

The SEC has proposed that Global's financial statements be revised to defer revenue for lifetime memberships and amortize it on a straight line basis over the estimated period which the member is expected to use the land and facilities.
Global said it has consulted with its accountants regarding the SEC proposal.
It said it expects to file a response to the SEC in the near future, but that it is uncertain what the ultimate determination will be.
